findings.what: Pinned derived artifacts are converted back to mutable pathnames before DuckDB opens them.
findings.why: Both lifecycle paths defeat their descriptor pin at the DuckDB boundary: build resolves the pinned staging descriptor to a pathname at lines 119-121, and verification resolves the pinned search descriptor at lines 214-215. A concurrent rename and symlink replacement after _descriptor_path returns can therefore make DuckDB write outside the private derived directory or open a different database. The post-open hash at lines 217-221 reads through the still-pinned directory descriptor, not the database object that DuckDB opened, so an attacker-controlled database can pass the old manifest/hash check and supply unverified rows. This is reachable under the same shared-case mutation model as the prior TOCTOU blocker, breaks AC2 containment and AC6 coherent hash binding, and is not exercised by the tests, which swap the search directory before _pin_search_root rather than after pathname conversion.

findings.what: The projection implementation still exceeds the maintainability boundary and combines unrelated responsibilities.
findings.why: The recovered module grew from the previously reported 566 lines to 789 lines, while the public search module is 285 lines. _signal_projection.py owns descriptor/path containment, manifest verification, canonical parsing, provenance and metadata policy, public mapping, DuckDB persistence, and staging. This remains six-month maintenance debt under the authoritative less-than-200-line module directive, but it is not itself a reachable correctness, security, data-loss, or acceptance failure, so it remains a follow-up rather than a blocker.

findings.what: The DuckDB file and manifest are still replaced separately despite the public atomic-rebuild claim.
findings.why: build_projection performs two independent os.replace calls at lines 137-148, while build_signal_projection still documents an atomic rebuild. Failure after the database replacement can leave a new database paired with the old manifest. Verification fails closed and a later explicit rebuild can recover without modifying canonical evidence, so this degenerate-filesystem edge remains a follow-up rather than a ship blocker; either publish one generation through a single atomic indirection or remove the inaccurate atomicity claim.
